title: Elenem — Sports Leagues SaaS
excerpt: A SaaS platform that helps sport leagues deploy websites, manage games and standings instantly.
intro: Elenem is a SaaS product that allows sport leagues and federations to deploy websites, manage games and engage fans quickly.
problem: Many local leagues lack the tools to publish fixtures, results and standings. Creating a production-ready site requires time, tooling and technical staff.
Leagues needed a way to increase fan engagement and drive revenue without expensive engineering work.
process: We interviewed league managers to understand pain points and the minimal data model required (teams, fixtures, results, standings).
Built a lightweight API and admin panel so non-technical staff could create fixtures and publish results in minutes.
Iterated on UI and performance, optimizing image delivery and caching for match-heavy pages.
solution: A modular Next.js frontend with a headless API that lets leagues spin up a site in minutes.
Realtime updates for scores and a minimal CMS to manage teams and competitions.
result: Improved fan engagement and provided an additional revenue stream for leagues. Early adopters reported increased website visits and easier matchday workflows.
lessons: Start with the smallest useful feature set — publishing fixtures and scores provided the largest immediate value.
Design for non-technical users first; good UX reduces support overhead.

title: Le Bourgeois — Travel Agency Platform
excerpt: A travel platform that aggregates schedules and prices to help travellers in the DRC make informed choices.
intro: Le Bourgeois is an intentional travel platform that aggregates airline schedules and fares to help travellers compare and book smartly.
problem: In the DRC region, airlines were not consistently listed on global distribution systems; travellers relied on agents and had poor visibility on prices and schedules.
The travel agency needed a way to increase online sales and reduce manual enquiries.
process: Built scrapers and normalizers to gather available schedule and pricing data from multiple sources.
Created a searchable, filterable frontend and an internal panel for the agency to manage listings and promotions.
solution: A data pipeline that normalizes fares and schedules and a modern front-end that presents comparisons quickly to travellers.
Tools for the agency to add promotions and convert enquiries into bookings.
result: The platform became a reference for travellers in the region, improving conversion rates and increasing trust in the agency.
lessons: Reliable data sources and a resilient scraping pipeline are essential when canonical APIs are missing.
Focus on conversion flows — search to booking must be frictionless.
